raw_text:
Beyond distance-, density-, and probabilistic-based methods, there are other approaches to clustering. One is graph-based clustering, which models data as a graph and identifies clusters based on the connections between nodes.
This is useful when the relationships among data points are more important than their physical distance.
Another is constraint-based clustering, which incorporates prior knowledge or predefined rules into the clustering process. For instance, some data points may be required to belong to same cluster, while others must be placed in different clusters. These approaches are especially helpful when standard methods cannot fully capture the true structure of the data.
